_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. Paths are relative to skills/proxmox/ once onboarded. Re-apply by hand or with the factory's handfix/apply_handfixes.py (kept with the cli-printing-press factory run, not in this repo; idempotent; exits non-zero if a hook site moved). A cross-spec regen (spec checksum changed) drops every client.go hook; a same-spec regen preserves them. internal/client/proxmox_routing_test.go fails if any hook is missing. tools-manifest.json (a library-only press artifact) is not vendored here, so its PBS-path fix is tracked only in the factory ledger.

handfixes.summary: PBS operations (generated with the placeholder origin https://localhost:8007) are routed to PROXMOX_PBS_HOST before the generated PROXMOX_BASE_URL rebase
handfixes.why: OpenAPI operation-level servers are not templated by the press, so every PBS command was baked to localhost:8007. Worse, the generated rebaseAbsoluteURLOntoOverride moves every absolute URL onto PROXMOX_BASE_URL, which would send PBS requests carrying the PBS token to the PVE host. Unconfigured PBS host errors instead; a loopback base stands in only under the Printing Press verify/dogfood harness. PVE bases must be https, except a loopback IP literal (a local stub, which never leaves the machine); TestPlainHTTPOnlyToLoopbackLiterals pins that rule.

handfixes.summary: The PBS per-operation Authorization header gets the PBSAPIToken= scheme prepended (bare USER@REALM!TOKENID:SECRET accepted)
handfixes.why: The press sends per-operation security-scheme headers raw and ignores x-auth-format on them, so a PBS request sent the bare token and got 401.

handfixes.summary: Self-signed Proxmox certificates are trusted by pinned SHA-256 fingerprint, bound per service: PROXMOX_TLS_FINGERPRINT pins only the PVE host and PROXMOX_PBS_TLS_FINGERPRINT only the PBS host (or per cluster in clusters.toml)
handfixes.why: Proxmox ships self-signed certificates and the generated client has no TLS option, so no command worked against a default install. Fingerprint pinning is Proxmox's own trust model (proxmox-backup-client uses PBS_FINGERPRINT). Pins are installed by a client hook (novel clusters.go via the generated registerClientHook) as a per-service transport, so a PVE pin can never vouch for the PBS host. There is deliberately no insecure mode.

asserts.contains: refusing to fall back to unpinned TLS

handfixes.summary: Responses shaped {data, total|digest|changes|active|success} are unwrapped like a bare {data} envelope
handfixes.why: The generated unwrapper only strips a one-key envelope (len == 1). Proxmox puts total next to data on task lists and logs and digest on config/job reads, so those responses reached commands and the store still wrapped.

handfixes.summary: Every auth-scheme decision goes through proxmoxAuthScheme, which forces PbsApiToken for PBS paths and the PBS host
handfixes.why: With --auth-preference PveApiToken the generated operationAuthScheme falls back to the PVE token for any request it cannot match to a PBS operation (redirects, absolute PBS URLs from code orchestration), which would send the PVE token to the PBS host.

handfixes.summary: Error messages and --dry-run show the routed PBS host instead of the placeholder https://localhost:8007
handfixes.why: Users debugging a PBS failure were told the CLI called localhost:8007, which is not where the request went.

handfixes.summary: guide.md (the vendored CLI README), SKILL.md, AGENTS.md and manifest.json carry Proxmox-correct env tables, exit codes, read-only statement and optional PBS/TLS settings (factory handfix/docs_patch.py)
handfixes.why: The templates claim PROXMOX_PBS_HOST is required, omit the TLS fingerprint and PBS token variables, advertise --stdin write input on a read-only CLI, and show a mock-value example; the Phase 4.8/4.9 doc audit flagged each. The press-generated manifest also names the MCP binary proxmox-pp-mcp, marks the PBS host required, defaults PROXMOX_HOST to localhost and omits both TLS fingerprint fields; onboard copies it from the source, so a reprint restores every one of those.

asserts.contains: Every command is read-only against Proxmox

handfixes.summary: A same-origin redirect to a PVE path keeps the PVE Authorization header the generated redirect handler just stamped
handfixes.why: The generated CheckRedirect stamps the primary-scheme header, then a second block deletes Authorization for every destination that is not the secondary (PBS) scheme, so a same-origin PVE hop arrived unauthenticated.

handfixes.summary: mcp-install.md env blocks and server.json environmentVariables name the real Proxmox variables: PROXMOX_HOST, PROXMOX_API_TOKEN and PROXMOX_TLS_FINGERPRINT to fill in, the three PROXMOX_PBS_* values optional and blank
handfixes.why: onboard.py generates both from the manifest env keys as '<your-...>' placeholders marked required and secret. A copy-pasted '<your-proxmox_pbs_host>' is a bogus PBS host, the generated block omitted the TLS fingerprint a stock (self-signed) Proxmox needs, and the registry card marked the hostnames secret and the optional PBS values required. A fleet docs re-mint regenerates mcp-install.md and would bring all of that back.

asserts.not_contains: credential for the Proxmox MCP server

handfixes.summary: `golang.org/x/text` is pinned at v0.41.0, above the press-emitted v0.39.0 that osv-scanner flags for GO-2026-6629
handfixes.why: Press 4.33.5 emits `golang.org/x/text v0.39.0` as an indirect dependency (modernc.org/sqlite). osv-scanner flags GO-2026-6629 (panic parsing crafted input in x/text/secure/precis) against it. It is presence-only today, but the fleet rule since 2026-10-14 is to ship above it, and a reprint from a press that still emits v0.39.0 silently restores the old version. Mirrors avanan's x-text-above-go-2026-5970 entry. Reprint 4.35.1 (2026-11-02): the render emits v0.39.0 again; raised to the fleet floor v0.42.0 (replay_handfixes floor), so the keep-assert moves from v0.41.0 to v0.42.0.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Raise the golang.org/x/text floor in the press module template (retro item against the generator).

handfixes.summary: sync refuses --path-context host=... and pbs_host=...: those keys choose the token-bearing origin, which the client already bound to its tokens, TLS pins and origin checks
handfixes.why: Generated sync.go writes --path-context values into Config.TemplateVars AFTER flags.newClient(), so CheckServiceOrigins and the per-service pins never saw the new host. `sync --path-context pbs_host=<attacker>` (also reachable as the MCP sync tool's path-context parameter) made the attacker the PBS host and sent it the PBS token; host= did the same for the PVE token. Only a pre-set pin stopped it. Found by the 2026-10-14 adversarial review with a live MCP repro. In this CLI the only path-context keys are those two origin vars, so the guard rejects every endpointTemplateVarSet key. internal/cli/credential_routing_behavior_test.go (TestPathContextCannotRepointTheHost) fails if the guard is removed. A ninth store-isolation sweep (2026-10-19) found a --path-context key filling a base-URL placeholder re-pointed sync after the store was scoped; such keys are refused (TestPathContextCannotRepointBaseURL).

asserts.contains: cannot change the Proxmox host: tokens and TLS pins are bound to the configured hosts

handfixes.summary: An unset PROXMOX_HOST leaves {host} unresolved (outside the Printing Press verify harness) instead of defaulting to localhost
handfixes.why: The spec's server-variable default made generated config.go fill {host} with localhost, so an operator who never set PROXMOX_HOST dialled https://localhost:8006 and got 'connection refused', and doctor could not tell the base URL was a placeholder (check_doctor_truth placeholder state). Unresolved, every request fails with 'PROXMOX_HOST not set; export PROXMOX_HOST=<value>' and doctor reports the placeholder with the fix. Verify mode keeps localhost so the press verifier still reaches Cobra.

handfixes.summary: doctor emits a negative credentials row when the client cannot be built, classifies a 404 at the health path as a wrong base URL, and names PROXMOX_HOST / PROXMOX_BASE_URL in the placeholder verdict, and reads the health path with GetWithHeadersNoCache
handfixes.why: check_doctor_truth (issue #282) failed proxmox in all four states: no credentials row on a client-init error, 'reachable (HTTP 404 at /)' against a host where the API path does not exist, and a placeholder verdict that never named the variable to set. Mirrors the doctor_verdict.go behaviour the fleet carries, applied as three narrow edits to the press 4.33.5 doctor.go, which already ships the placeholder check and client.ProbeGet. The health probe also went through the generated 5-minute GET cache, so doctor could report a host reachable from a cached answer after it went down.

handfixes.summary: proxmox_execute refuses any non-GET endpoint whether or not PROXMOX_MCP_READ_ONLY is set
handfixes.why: The connector is read-only toward Proxmox by design (an MSP owner: 'I dont let AI near my hypervisors'), but the generated execute handler keeps live POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE branches and refuses them only under the opt-in read-only switch. Today every codeOrchEndpoints entry is a GET, so read-only rested on one generated table with no guard: a reprint that admitted one write endpoint would make it callable over MCP. The refusal sits in the handler, ahead of the switch check, so the generated codeOrchBlockedByMCPReadOnly test keeps its meaning. TestCodeOrchIsGetOnly asserts every table entry is GET and that an injected POST is refused; reverting the guard makes it fail.

handfixes.summary: The root --help highlights and the which index say capacity forecasts only PBS datastores, restore-points claims no prune prediction, and restore-points exit 5 also means no readable point while a source was unread
handfixes.why: The press copies the research novel-feature descriptions into root.go. Two overclaimed: capacity has no forecast for PVE storage (only PBS computes estimated-full-date), and pruneMarks runs only on PVE storage listings, so PBS-API points carry no prune mark. Round-2 adversarial review (2026-10-15) flagged both as claims the binary does not deliver. which.go carries the same novel-feature text (plus the restore-points exit-code note) and drifted the same way; adversarial round 5 caught the exit-5 contradiction against restore-points --help. Codex round 22 and adversarial round 12 (2026-10-15) found the prune prediction itself unsound (vzdump backs up before it prunes, per-node storages across migrations, storage aliases of one PBS datastore), so restore-points stopped predicting prunes and every description of it (root.go, which.go, the MCP insight in tools.go) drops the claim. Codex round 23 found capacity's unpruned flag a retention-absence claim built on one cluster's jobs, so capacity stopped asserting it and every description drops 'prune state'. The merge-gate Codex review (2026-10-16) found the MCP command-mirror description in tools.go still carried the PVE forecast overclaim.

handfixes.summary: Every successful JSON response passes through redactSecretFields before the generated client returns it, so secret-named fields never reach the HTTP cache, the local store, the search index, or any CLI or MCP output
handfixes.why: GET /storage returns a storage plugin's storage.cfg entry verbatim, and third-party plugins (freenas-proxmox and similar) keep passwords and API keys there. The generated client cached and stored the body as-is, and the MCP sql/search/execute tools returned it. Found by adversarial round 7 with a sentinel secret; TestStorageSecretsRedacted and client TestRedactSecretFields pin it.

handfixes.summary: proxmox_execute and the posture recipe tool advertise readOnlyHint=true / destructiveHint=false (mcp-go defaults a tool to destructive)
handfixes.why: Every code-orchestration endpoint is a GET and execute refuses anything else (code-orch-get-only), but the generated tools carried mcp-go's default hints, so an MCP client gating on hints treated every Proxmox read as a destructive write. Found by adversarial round 7; internal/mcp/read_only_hints_test.go pins it.

handfixes.summary: Three upstream apidoc summaries that name the wrong operation are corrected in the generated command, the MCP endpoint table, SKILL.md and guide.md
handfixes.why: proxmox-backup's doc comments put 'Add a TOTP secret to the user' over the GET that lists a user's TFA entries, 'List all datastores' over the network-interface list, and 'Get named known ACME directory endpoints' over the challenge-schema read. In a read-only connector the first reads as a secret-writing call. A reprint from the same apidoc brings them back.

asserts.contains: List a user's TFA entries (types and descriptions; no secrets).
Get the ACME challenge plugin schema.

asserts.not_contains: Add a TOTP secret to the user

handfixes.summary: configureDefaultDBScope keys the local store by the selected clusters.toml entry (--cluster / PROXMOX_CLUSTER), so each client cluster has its own data.db
handfixes.why: The generated store scope comes from the env/config credential, fixed before the selected cluster's token is applied, so every --cluster wrote into one store: colliding VMIDs overwrote another client's rows, and an unreachable cluster's read fell back to another client's data labelled source=local. Found by adversarial round 7; TestLocalStoreIsPerCluster pins it. The merge-gate Codex review (2026-10-16) found the name alone shared one store across two clusters files (or a clusters add --force replacement) that reuse a name for another client; the key now carries the clusters file path and the entry's endpoints (not the client label, so a rename keeps local-only data), and an entry with no endpoint identity gets a per-process store no later invocation reopens. TestReusedClusterNameGetsItsOwnStore and TestUnresolvedClusterNeverReopensAStore pin it. A second merge-gate review found config.Load errors returned before the cluster scope was applied, so a malformed config.toml put every cluster in one unscoped store; the cluster scope is now decided first (TestConfigErrorKeepsClusterStoresApart). A fourth sweep found one private address reused behind another VPN for a different client kept the store; every connection field (token references and certificate fingerprints too) is now identity, only the client label is not (TestReusedPrivateAddressWithNewCredentialsGetsItsOwnStore). The merge-gate review (2026-10-19) found token env names but not their values in the identity, so the same entry behind another VPN with new token values reopened the previous client's store; SHA-256 digests of the resolved token values are now part of it (TestNewTokenValuesGetTheirOwnStore).

handfixes.summary: The generated response cache is off (proxmoxNoResponseCache): no read is answered from it or written to it, because Proxmox answers carry free-text notes and comments where MSPs keep credentials, and a backup-assurance tool must not answer from a 5-minute-old copy
handfixes.why: Generated client.go caches every fresh GET on disk for 5 minutes, so VM/node/pool descriptions, backup notes, PBS snapshot comments and notes persisted in 0600 files. The 2026-10-16 adversarial reviews (rounds 20-22) and Codex round 34 found them there; a path allowlist missed every PBS read (absolute https://host:8007 URLs) and every comment-bearing endpoint nobody listed, so the cache is off at its single gate (responseCacheEnabled), which also stops a stale file from an older version being served. internal/cli/codex_round31_test.go (TestVMConfigNotCached) fails if any response cache file is written by the PVE and PBS reads it drives.

handfixes.summary: A PVE endpoint from one run's environment (PROXMOX_BASE_URL, PROXMOX_HOST, --cluster) is never saved to config.toml; when PROXMOX_HOST names another host:port than a saved base_url, or an endpoint is ambiguous ('@' after '/'), no PVE (or PBS) request is sent; no endpoint keeps a user:password@ part
handfixes.why: Generated config.go persisted the runtime BaseURL and TemplateVars on every save, so `auth set-token` run with PROXMOX_BASE_URL wrote that host into config.toml, and every later env-configured run sent its own token there, ignoring PROXMOX_HOST: client B's token reached client A's host (2026-10-16 adversarial round 24, reproduced against a stub that logged the Authorization header). configForSave now keeps the file's endpoints; Load records an EndpointRefusal when PROXMOX_HOST names another host:port than a base_url saved without {host} (default port 8006; round 26 found a host-only compare let a port mismatch through), and doInternal in generated client.go refuses every PVE request with it, so auth logout and --cluster runs (which clear it) still work, and strips user:password@ from every endpoint so it is never sent or printed (endpoint_userinfo.go). internal/config/endpoints_env_only_test.go fails if any part is removed. Round 29: an ambiguous PROXMOX_PBS_HOST is refused (PBSRefusal, enforced in doInternal for PBS requests), never replaced by a pbs_host saved in config.toml, and ambiguous endpoints are stored only redacted so doctor cannot print them.

handfixes.summary: A per-endpoint read that answers from the local mirror because Proxmox could not be reached warns on stderr in every output form (the JSON meta.source label is lost in --csv, --plain and --quiet)
handfixes.why: Generated data_source.go falls back to the local SQLite mirror on a network error and labels it only in the JSON envelope, so `backup job --csv` after a sync printed a stale job row, exit 0, with nothing marking it (2026-10-16 adversarial round 24). Both fallback sites now call warnMirrorAnswer (internal/cli/mirror_answer.go). internal/cli/adversarial_round24_test.go (TestMirrorAnswerWarnsInEveryForm) fails if the call is removed.

handfixes.summary: PersistentPreRunE re-scopes the local store after a saved run profile is applied, so a profile's saved --cluster or --config gets that tenant's store
handfixes.why: The generated pre-run scopes the store before ApplyProfileToFlags, so two profiles saved with different --cluster values reached different tenants but both read and wrote the default store: rows could overwrite each other and answer for another tenant. Found by the merge-gate Codex review (2026-10-16); TestSavedProfileClusterGetsItsOwnStore pins it.

handfixes.summary: With a cluster selected, every local store path derives from that cluster's scope: legacy data.db adoption and ownership markers are skipped, a missing HOME still yields a scoped file, any --db (including whitespace or a saved profile's db) is refused, a store path SQLite would truncate at '?' or '#' is refused, a namespace-only entry is unresolved, and flag-correction learning never runs when pre-run did not scope the store; and one process binds one read of the entry for both the API client and the store
handfixes.why: A Codex class sweep of every store open (2026-10-16) found four ways two clusters still resolved to one file: unproven .owner ownership fell back to the shared data.db, help and parse-failure paths opened the learn store before pre-run scoped it, HOME unset returned a bare data.db, and an explicit or profile-supplied --db named one shared file. Pinned by TestClusterStoreIgnoresLegacyUnscopedDB, TestClusterStoreWithoutPreRun, TestClusterStoreWithoutHome, TestDBFlagRefusedWithCluster. A second sweep found a profile's cluster unapplied on the help path, a whitespace --db, a '?' in the data directory truncating the SQLite DSN, and a namespace-only entry keeping a reusable identity; each now fails closed (TestDBFlagRefusedWithCluster, TestClusterStorePathWithQueryCharRefused, TestNamespaceOnlyEntryIsUnresolved). A third sweep found the store re-read clusters.toml per call, so a clusters add --force during a request moved the store to the new tenant while the client kept the old endpoint; entries are now snapshotted once per process (TestClusterEntryBoundForTheProcess). The fourth sweep also found '%' escapes decoded by the read-only file: URI; '%' and control characters are refused with '?' and '#'. A seventh sweep found the no-home fallback still returned a bare data.db without a cluster and an explicit --db escaped the URI-syntax rule; the fallback is always scoped and --db is checked (TestEnvStoreWithoutHomeAndExplicitDBSyntax). The eighth sweep also found a clusters.toml address could carry a {placeholder} filled from config.toml; such addresses are refused.

handfixes.summary: Without a cluster, the target's store is always scoped by credentials plus effective endpoints and TLS pins (even with no token loaded), an unreadable config gets a per-process store, a client built from a different config read than pre-run's is refused, store paths with URI syntax are refused, and a scoped store never adopts data.db or a legacy file
handfixes.why: The generated store scope hashed the credential alone, so the same token aimed at another PROXMOX_HOST fell back to the first host's rows (auto fallback and --data-source local). proxmox shipped with endpoint-aware scoping, so legacy adoption has nothing to migrate and is ambiguous by construction. Found by the merge-gate Codex review (2026-10-19); TestEnvStoreFollowsEndpoint and TestEnvStoreIgnoresLegacyUnscopedDB pin it. The generated MCP test that expected adoption of an existing data.db now asserts the scoped path. A sixth sweep found the no-cluster path still shared stores when no token was loaded, on a config-load error, under a '?' data directory, and when the config was replaced between pre-run and client creation; each now fails closed (TestEnvStoreFailsClosed, TestClientRefusedWhenConfigChangedMidRun). Generated MCP path tests now expect the scoped data-<hash>.db. An eighth sweep found template variables that fill a base-URL placeholder missing from the identity; every template variable now counts (TestTemplateVarsAreStoreIdentity).

handfixes.summary: The two derive-lock tests (ContendedAppendIsDerivedBeforeReturn, CaughtUpPassDoesNotWait) wait on what the pass is doing, read from goroutine stacks, instead of fixed 200 ms, 500 ms and 5 s windows; every remaining wait is bounded by the test binary's own deadline
handfixes.why: On windows(fortinet) in CI (2026-10-22, PR #421) the contended test failed with 'contended pass did not finish after the peer released the lock': after release the pass opens a fresh SQLite store and commits, and a slow Windows runner took longer than the fixed 5 s. The 200 ms 'did not return while held' window was also weak: on a slow runner it could elapse before the pass even reached the wait. The contended test now waits until the pass is provably blocked in cliutil.WithFileLock called from DeriveFlagCorrections (it cannot return before release), so it is stronger, not weaker. Proven: a pass that returns early under contention fails it; a caught-up pass that polls or blocks fails the caught-up test; with a simulated 6 s store open after the lock, the old test fails with the CI message and the new one passes.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the generated internal/learn derive_test.go should use this state-based wait in place of the fixed windows.

handfixes.summary: the spec declares x-pp-mutation: false on ten documented Proxmox GET reads whose names (scan, sync, cmd-safety) press 4.35.1 classifies as mutating
handfixes.why: Reprint 4.35.1 (2026-11-02). 4.35.1 classifies GET operations by name: /nodes/{node}/scan{,/lvm,/lvmthin,/zfs}, /nodes/{node}/ceph/cmd-safety and PBS /admin/sync, /config/sync{,/{id}}, /tape/scan-changers, /tape/scan-drives became mutating, so the CLI called GetMutating (verify short-circuits it) and the MCP surface moved them behind a new proxmox_execute + confirm tool whose default hints are destructive, on a connector that never writes. Each is a read in the official apidoc (x-source on each operation). x-pp-mutation: false is the press's own per-operation override, so the fix lives in the spec and survives reprints; with it the 4.35.1 render registers no proxmox_execute tool and the ten commands read through the normal resolveReadWithStrategy path. TestToolsAdvertiseReadOnly fails on the unrepaired render (proxmox_execute destructive).
handfixes.spec-encode: Done in the library spec.yaml (reprint bin/prep.sh). Fold it into cli-factory/proxmox/spec/build_spec.py before the next print.

handfixes.summary: SetServicePins keeps the press's TLS trust (--ca-cert / PROXMOX_CA_CERT, --tls-server-name) for a service with no fingerprint pin; a pin still replaces it for that service only
handfixes.why: Reprint 4.35.1 (2026-11-02). 4.35.1 adds --ca-cert and --tls-server-name to the generated transport. The per-service pin hook cloned that transport and then set TLSClientConfig = strictPinConfig(...), which is nil without pins, so an unpinned PVE or PBS dropped the CA and server name: an MSP with an internal CA got 'x509: unknown authority' and doctor still reported the ca-cert. Fails closed (no leak), but the advertised flag did nothing. Now the clone keeps the press config unless that service has pins. TestUnpinnedServiceKeepsCACert failed first (logs/seen/unpinned-ca-cert-fails.log).

handfixes.summary: the MCP HTTP-transport bearer token is read through cliutil.EnvOverride, and EffectiveEnv treats a whitespace-padded unresolved ${...} template as unset, so an MCPB placeholder is never accepted as the secret
handfixes.why: Reprint 4.35.1 (2026-11-02). The skill manifest maps PROXMOX_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN to ${user_config.proxmox_mcp_http_token}; a host that leaves the template unresolved passes that public 37-character literal, and 4.35.1's requireHTTPCallerToken read it with os.Getenv and accepted it (32-character minimum), so --transport http could start off loopback with a publicly known bearer. Codex 2026-11-02 r1 found the padded form ' ${...} ' passed EffectiveEnv too (checked before trimming); the check now trims, in the one helper every env read uses. GENERATED cmd/proxmox-pp-mcp/main.go and internal/cliutil/verifyenv.go, re-applied by the reprint's bin/reapply.py. Both tests failed first (logs/seen/).

handfixes.summary: cross-cluster collision detection identifies a network share or an unpinned PBS by every spelling of its host (name plus resolved addresses), so a NAS named by host in one cluster and by IP in another is one share; a host name that does not resolve on this machine has unknown identity and overlaps every share of the same type and path (an unpinned PBS name joins every PBS on its port)
handfixes.why: Codex review 2026-11-02 round 1 (P1, wrong cluster or store; GET /nodes/{node}/storage/{storage}/content rows carry a VMID but no originating cluster). netStorageID keyed NFS/CIFS/CephFS/Gluster shares by the configured server spelling, so client A mounting nas.example:/backups and client B mounting 10.0.0.9:/backups were judged distinct and B's VM 100 archive counted as A's VM 100 restore point. One shared hostAliases (canonHost + LookupHost addresses, cached, 2 s) now feeds netStorageID and the PBS serviceTokens; resolution only adds spellings, so sharing is detected more often, never less. TestShareIdentityFollowsHostAddresses / TestPBSServiceFollowsHostAddresses failed first (logs/seen/r1-host-alias-fails.log). Round 2 (P1, same class): a name this machine cannot resolve kept one spelling, so nas.client.lan in one cluster and 10.0.0.9 in another still looked like two shares. Fail closed: hostUnknown marks the share token (unknownHostMark, matched by tokenMatch in overlaps and netMounters, the peer named with the unresolved host) and pbsServices.joinUnknown merges an unresolved unpinned PBS endpoint with every PBS on its port, called once in markSharedPBS. TestUnresolvedShareHostIsNotProofOfDistinctShares / TestUnresolvedUnpinnedPBSIsNotProofOfDistinctServices failed first (logs/seen/r2-fix-red.log).

handfixes.summary: README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json say the ChatGPT desktop app runs this connector locally (STDIO) and that ChatGPT on the web, Microsoft 365 Copilot / Copilot Studio and the Gemini app are not supported by msp-skills yet, with a link to the hosted-gateway comparison; no paid-plan list, no Developer Mode recipe, no 'ChatGPT connects only to remote servers'.
handfixes.why: Docs fix approved 2026-11-03, following PR #502. OpenAI's MCP docs (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp) say the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI and the IDE extension support MCP servers, add them as STDIO, and share MCP configuration; ChatGPT on the web uses remote MCP through plugins and does not read local Codex config. The old text listed ChatGPT plans, said ChatGPT connects only to remote servers, and on the reprinted connectors told users to host the connector over HTTPS for a Developer Mode connector and Copilot Studio; SECURITY.md pauses HTTP mode until each connector is reprinted. handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand: internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one credkit.Declarations literal; both mains start with credkit.Start(credwire.Declarations) and end with credkit.Exit; every HTTP client (API, per-service TLS pins, --deliver webhook and Spacefast, feedback, probe) goes through credkit.Transport, every SQLite handle through the credkit.SQLDriver internal/credsql registers, every program file write through the kit, child processes through credkit.RunCommand or StartCommand, and the MCP stdio and HTTP servers through credkit.MCPTools, MCPIn, MCPOut and MCPHTTP. A Proxmox token is USER@REALM!TOKENID=SECRET (PBS: ...:SECRET); only the SECRET is held (cliutil.TokenSecret), under minted:pve-token, minted:pbs-token or minted:cluster:<home>:<name>:<service>, each bound to that token's own origin (PVE base URL or PROXMOX_HOST, PROXMOX_PBS_HOST, each clusters.toml entry's own hosts); the raw env, config and Authorization forms are exempt with that reason, because Proxmox lists the token id in ordinary reads. The credential store and config are sources, written outside the kit.
handfixes.why: One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks; proxmox had no earlier credential layer (no funnel, no holder). response-secret-redaction stays: storage plugins name their own secret fields, which an exact-name ResponseFields list cannot cover. Classes closed, each by a built-binary test in internal/credwire/leak_test.go seen failing first on the pre-kit build (.review/seen-fail-kit.log): an API error echoing part of the token secret (CLI, --agent, MCP); tokens in config.toml, the credential store and a config that does not parse held at startup; PROXMOX_API_TOKEN, PROXMOX_PBS_API_TOKEN and clusters.toml tokens held at startup; each token sent only to its own service or cluster, never to a --deliver webhook; SPACEFAST_TOKEN held; and the learn journal never recording a held secret. TestTokenIDInOrdinaryReadIsShown failed on a build that held whole tokens: a task list naming root@pam!monitor printed only the kit's notice.
